name: Kimpton Fitzroy London
positioning: Historic hotel on Russell Square in Bloomsbury, built as Hotel Russell in 1900, with Titanic-linked history and a pet-friendly policy
best_for: Travelers who want a historic base in Bloomsbury next to Russell Square

facts.text: Hotel Russell was the first hotel in London to have en suite bathrooms.
The hotel occupies the entire eastern side of Russell Square Gardens.
The bedrooms were designed by Tara Bernerd & Partners.
Fitz's Bar is reached through an unassuming side door.
The Terrace is a seasonal outdoor bar and restaurant inspired by the Italian Riviera.
Pets stay at no additional charge and no deposit is required.
There is no size or weight limit for pets, and no limit on the number of pets.
The fitness centre has Peloton exercise bikes, Technogym cardio machines and free weights.
The hosted Social Hour offers complimentary wine, beer and soft drinks.
A complimentary Bloomsbury walking tour is offered on Sundays.
Bloomsbury is home to the British Museum and many boutiques and bookshops.
The entrance has statues of four British queens and the lobby floor has a zodiac mosaic.

highlights.text: The building was designed by Charles Fitzroy Doll in 1898, who also designed the dining room on the Titanic.
Afternoon tea is served in the room said to have inspired the Titanic's first-class dining saloon.
Fitz's Bar has ostrich feathers, Victorian curiosities, a fireplace and a mirrorball.
The Bloomsbury Suites sit within the hotel's turrets and have panoramic views of Russell Square.
A tarot reading experience is offered in partnership with Treadwell's of Bloomsbury.

considerations.text: There is no local area shuttle at the hotel.
There are no airport shuttles to Heathrow, Gatwick or London City airports.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing typical of central London luxury hotels.
